sentence: She needs to brush ___ on her Spanish before the trip.
explanation: El phrasal verb <brush up on> significa repasar o mejorar una habilidad que no has usado recientemente.
tip: She wants to review and improve her Spanish skills.

sentence: They decided to call ___ the wedding.
explanation: El phrasal verb <call off> significa cancelar.
tip: They cancelled the event.

sentence: He came ___ with a great idea for the campaign.
explanation: El phrasal verb <come up with> significa pensar en o sugerir una idea o plan.
tip: He invented or thought of a great idea.

sentence: I can't put ___ with his attitude anymore.
explanation: El phrasal verb <put up with> significa tolerar a alguien o algo desagradable.
tip: He can't tolerate his attitude anymore.

sentence: She takes ___ her mother; they are very similar.
explanation: El phrasal verb <take after> significa parecerse a un familiar mayor.
tip: She resembles her mother — they look alike.

sentence: The negotiations broke ___ without an agreement.
explanation: El phrasal verb <break down> puede significar dejar de funcionar o fracasar.
tip: The talks failed — they collapsed.

sentence: I ran ___ an old friend at the supermarket.
explanation: El phrasal verb <run into> significa encontrarse con alguien por casualidad.
tip: I met someone unexpectedly at the supermarket.

sentence: He promised to look ___ my cat while I'm away.
explanation: El phrasal verb <look after> significa cuidar de alguien o algo.
tip: He promised to take care of the cat.

sentence: We need to get ___ to the real issue here.
explanation: El phrasal verb <get down to> significa empezar a hacer o considerar algo seriamente.
tip: Focus on the real issue — start dealing with it seriously.

sentence: She finally got ___ her fear of flying.
explanation: El phrasal verb <get over> significa recuperarse de una enfermedad, sorpresa o miedo.
tip: She conquered her fear — which particle completes "get ___" to mean recover?

sentence: The company is looking ___ new employees.
explanation: El phrasal verb <look for> significa buscar.
tip: The company is seeking new employees — which particle completes 'look ___'?

sentence: The plane will take ___ in ten minutes.
explanation: El phrasal verb <take off> significa despegar (para aviones) o quitarse (ropa).
tip: The plane will leave the ground soon.

sentence: It's cold, you should put ___ a jacket.
explanation: El phrasal verb <put on> significa ponerse ropa.
tip: You wear a jacket when it's cold.

sentence: Please go ___ with your story, I'm listening.
explanation: El phrasal verb <go on> significa continuar o seguir.
tip: Continue telling your story — don't stop.

sentence: I hope everything works ___ for you.
explanation: El phrasal verb <work out> significa resolver un problema o tener éxito.
tip: I hope everything goes well / succeeds — which particle completes 'work ___'?

sentence: I came ___ an old photo album while cleaning.
explanation: El phrasal verb <come across> significa encontrar algo o a alguien por casualidad.
tip: I found an old photo album by chance while cleaning.

sentence: She needs to fill ___ this form before she leaves.
explanation: El phrasal verb <fill in> o <fill out> significa rellenar un formulario.
tip: Complete the form — write the required information.

sentence: They decided to eat ___ tonight instead of cooking.
explanation: El phrasal verb <eat out> significa comer fuera de casa.
tip: They chose to eat at a restaurant instead of cooking.

sentence: She needs to put ___ her clothes after washing them.
explanation: El phrasal verb <put away> significa guardar algo en su lugar.
tip: Store the clothes in their proper place after washing.

sentence: He needs to throw ___ his old shoes.
explanation: El phrasal verb <throw away> o <throw out> significa desechar algo.
tip: Get rid of the old shoes — discard them.
